subject: English
passage: One challenge faced by scientists studying coral reef ecosystems is that different marine research organizations have different criteria for what determines a healthy reef. Many organizations classify reef health based on the percentage of live coral cover present. However, organizations do not all use the same threshold; for example, the Caribbean Marine Institute uses a minimum of 30% coral cover, while the Great Barrier Reef Foundation uses 60%. Other organizations use a combination of coral cover and additional factors, like water temperature and species biodiversity. This inconsistency makes it difficult for scientists to compare aspects of reef health across different regions.
prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Scientists focus on factors other than coral cover when conducting studies on reef health in the Caribbean.
choices.B: Even though organizations use different methods to classify healthy reefs, scientists consider any reef having at least 60% coral cover to be healthy.
choices.C: It is difficult for scientists to compare aspects of reef health globally because of the various ways different organizations classify healthy reefs.
choices.D: Reef health is easily compared between regions when they have similar water temperatures.

explanation: Choice C is the best answer because it most accurately states the main idea of the text. The passage opens by identifying that different organizations have different criteria for determining healthy reefs, then provides specific examples: the Caribbean Marine Institute uses 30% coral cover while the Great Barrier Reef Foundation uses 60%, and some organizations use additional factors like water temperature and biodiversity. The text concludes that this inconsistency makes it difficult for scientists to compare reef health across different regions. Choice C synthesizes these elements—the difficulty in comparison, the global scope, and the cause (various classification methods).
